previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A  woman with a history of neurogenic bladder from a prior gunshot wound, urostomy placement earlier in the year, type II diabetes, and right below-knee amputation was admitted for new-onset pain around her urostomy site and gross hematuria. She had no fever or leukocytosis, and initial urinalysis showed blood and white cells but urine culture revealed fecal contamination rather than true infection. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed no nephrolithiasis or fluid collection, ruling out stones or abscess. The clinical picture was consistent with urostomy site inflammation. Pain and hematuria resolved during the hospital stay with supportive care, and antibiotics were discontinued. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, instructions for follow-up with primary care and urology, and a plan for ongoing stoma and pain management.

INDICATION:  ___ s/p multiple self-inflicted stabs to urostomy, now s/p exlap,

urostomy. Thanks

TECHNIQUE:  Loopogram

COMPARISON:  None available

FINDINGS: 

Initial AP scout images prior to administration of contrast show a foley
catheter within the ileal conduit.

Intermittent fluoroscopy was performed while approximately 100 cc of
Cysto-Conray water soluble contrast was instilled through the patient's
catheter. Instillation was terminated when the ileal loop was completely full,
at which time there was no evidence of contrast leakage. No ureteral contrast
reflux was seen.
An additional 40cc of normal saline was then instilled into the ileal loop.
The patient's catheter was then reconnected to the urinary bag.

Fluoroscopic images also demonstrate several moderately distended loops of
small bowel.

IMPRESSION: 

1. No evidence of leak from the ileal conduit.
2. Several moderately distended loops of small bowel, likely representing
functional postoperative ileus.
